>> This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
The president of Cornell University says the school must do better amid criticism
of its handling of rape allegations on campus.
In a video released on Saturday, Michael Kotlikoff acknowledged frustration
over how little Cornell has said publicly about its response.
>> There are real legal and privacy limits on what we can say.
But we will make a greater effort to explain what we can to provide context
about the actions Cornell has taken and to be more transparent.
>> A former student alleges she was gang raped at a fraternity house in 2024.
The university says its trustees will announce this week
which outside law firm will independently review the school's handling of the case.
Students and parents will also have opportunities in the coming weeks
to bring their concerns directly to Cornell's leadership.
President Trump says he won't ban U.S. diesel exports to Europe
after G7 countries announced Friday they would release 100 million barrels
of diesel and crude oil from national reserves.
Terry Schultz reports Trump pressured the European members of the group to make the move
to help ease fuel prices in the U.S. ahead of the midterm elections.
The G7 which includes the four biggest European economies plus the European Union agreed
to tap emergency inventories after President Trump demanded they help curb the rise
of fuel prices caused primarily by the U.S. war on Iran.
European leaders had been reluctant to contribute from their fuel stocks.
Analyst Maximilian Terhale of Cambridge University Center for Geopolitics says they should have
used the situation to remind the often critical Trump that he needs them as allies.
It's somewhat desperate and we need to, in a friendly way, manipulate that desperation.
It's not clear how much of the fuel will come from each country's reserves
to make up the announced 100 million barrels.
For NPR News, I'm Terry Schultz in Brussels.
The window is closing for registering to vote in the midterm elections in some parts
of the country and PR's Hansi Lo Wang has a rundown of the deadlines voters need to know.
This weekend is the last chance for eligible voters to register
or update their registration in Alaska, Rhode Island and the U.S. Virgin Islands.
In South Carolina, online sign-ups end Sunday and the state's postmark deadline for mail-in
applications is Monday.
Monday is also the voter registration deadline for American Samoa, Arizona, Indiana and Ohio,
plus many southern states.
They include Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Mississippi, Tennessee and Texas.
Then in Missouri, voter registration for the midterm elections closes on Wednesday.
If you're already registered, you can confirm your status by visiting your state or territory's
official election website.
Election officials recommend checking before the deadline, especially if you recently moved,
changed your name or haven't voted in a while.
Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News.
This is NPR News in Washington.
Tennessee's prison chief is resigning as the state reviews Wednesday's failed execution
of inmate Christa Pike.
Governor Bill Lee announced the departure of Frank Strada yesterday, calling it a difficult
moment.
Pike's lawyers say she's unconscious and on a ventilator in a hospital, they say medical
staff were working to clear two doses of an execution drug from her system.
Several artificial intelligence data centers are planned for Louisiana.
Many communities there have been resistant to the facilities in part because of their
use of power and water resources.
Barbara Uhouse of the Gulf States newsroom reports that community colleges are preparing
local residents for new jobs.
At Louisiana Delta Community College in Monroe, about a dozen students are learning to build
and maintain data centers.
I'm going to pass around some safety glasses.
Local businesses often rely on community colleges to provide the training people need to work
for them.
In Northeast Louisiana, the biggest business right now is meta.
The tech giant is building its largest data center here and it needs thousands of workers.
Since January, more than 100 people have graduated from Delta's new programs, which they launched
with meta support.
The college says all of the graduates are working.
Some thought they'd have to leave the area to find work and say they're glad to have
an option closer to home.
For NPR news, I'm Opera Uhouse, I'm Windsor Johnston and you're listening to NPR News from Washington.
This message comes from U.S. Bank.
Chief Product Officer Shruti Patel shares why U.S. Bank Business Essentials is designed
to bring together the key products small business owners need.
Some of our small business owners were telling us how complicated it was, having checking
in one place will pay in another and so our goal was to help business owners bring it all
together by building business essentials.
This was really to help business owners focus more on growing their business.
Learn more at usbank.com/businessmemberfdic
